requirements.evidence: Migrations match the contract: cascading FKs, unique (queue_id, code), the recommended index, and called_by_user_id nullOnDelete (create_tickets_table.php:16-28). Queue/Ticket models, enums, InactiveQueueException and Entity::queues() are present. IssueTicket rejects negative priority, then lock-re-reads the queue inside the transaction ('Queue::query()->lockForUpdate()->findOrFail', IssueTicket.php:36-40) and retries up to 3 times on UniqueConstraintViolationException. Ticket::nextCode walks codes by id desc and skips malformed ones with an anchored regex (Ticket.php:72-84). The write-once guard runs in the updating hook (Ticket.php:46-55). call() authorizes, re-checks status under a lock and records the caller. The factory allocates codes per ticket and supports forQueue and explicit codes (TicketFactory.php:36-50). One gap: deleting the newest ticket frees its number, which the docblock admits ('not reused unless they were the newest', Ticket.php:70). That conflicts with the general rule 'deleting a ticket does not reuse its number'.

conventions.evidence: Domain write goes through the invokable App\Actions\IssueTicket. Authorization uses a policy (app/Policies/TicketPolicy.php) via Gate::forUser()->authorize. Mass assignment is set deliberately with #[Fillable]. Migrations have down(). docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md, docs/architecture.md and CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] are updated, and public methods have PHPDoc. Small deviation: the domain write Ticket::call() lives on the model rather than in an Action. The task contract asks for exactly that, so this is minor.

security.evidence: call() authorizes before any write (Ticket.php:95) and the policy checks membership in the ticket's entity, resolved from the database (TicketPolicy.php:15-17). The status re-check under lockForUpdate prevents a double call through stale instances. Fillable excludes called_at and called_by_user_id, which are set only via forceFill inside call(). There is no HTTP or Livewire surface, so there is no client input to validate.

tests.evidence: Four Pest files cover: defaults; container resolution; sequential codes; A999→A1000→A1001; middle deletion; malformed and lookalike codes (dataset, including trailing newline and overflow); per-queue uniqueness; inactive and stale-deactivated queues with nothing persisted; retry and give-up on collisions (IssueTicketTest.php:94-122); write-once for every immutable field via save and update (TicketWriteOnceTest.php:15-31); single call; stale double call; non-member AuthorizationException with the ticket unchanged; cascade deletes; and factory batch codes. No test covers deleting the newest ticket, which is the one gap.

simplicity.evidence: Lean overall: a small action with a bounded retry loop, an updating hook with a MUTABLE allow-list, and a short nextCode loop. Minor redundancy: call() checks status before the transaction and again inside it (Ticket.php:97-105). The inner locked check alone would be enough after authorization.

readability.evidence: Names are clear (MAX_ATTEMPTS, MUTABLE) and comments explain intent ('Lock + re-read: the caller's instance may predate a deactivation.'; 'Up to 15 digits keeps the number inside a native int.'). Methods are short and focused, and factories and models follow the standard generated layout. There is no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task. TicketPolicy supports the required membership check. The one-line edit to docs/architecture.md (adding `status` to the mutable fields) keeps the docs consistent with the implemented rule. There is no UI, API or call-next logic.

issues.explanation: nextCode derives the next number from the newest surviving ticket, so deleting the latest ticket (e.g. A003 of A001..A003) reissues A003. This contradicts 'deleting a ticket does not reuse its number', and the docblock and docs narrow the rule to 'in the middle' instead of fixing it.
Only middle-ticket deletion is tested; there is no test for deleting the newest ticket, which is where number reuse actually happens.
The pre-transaction status check duplicates the locked re-check inside the transaction.
The call write and its authorization live on the model rather than in an app/Actions class. The task contract requires this, but it differs from the 'domain writes go through Actions' convention.

review.summary: Adds queues and tickets with migrations, models, enums, factories, a membership policy, the IssueTicket action (locked re-read of the queue and collision retry), write-once enforcement and single-call semantics, plus thorough Pest tests and updated docs and changelog. Almost every requirement and edge case is met. The one real gap is that deleting the newest ticket lets its number be reissued, so I would approve with a small follow-up.
